articles.title: Three church killings suspects held in Jordan shootout
articles.excerpt: Jordanian security forces have arrested three suspects in connection with an attack on a church in the US-allied country that…
articles.fullText:
Jordanian security forces have arrested three suspects in connection with an attack on a church in the US-allied country that killed nine people, state television reported on Monday.

The attack, in which gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church on Friday in the village of Hamoud in Karak governorate, about 120 kilometres southwest of the capital Amman, also wounded 40 others.

The shooting lasted several minutes, witnesses said.

Jordan's Public Security Directorate said security forces located the three suspects early on Monday hiding in an abandoned house in Karak.

The suspects refused to surrender and opened fire on security forces, who returned fire and arrested all three after they were wounded, the directorate said in a statement carried on state media.

No security personnel were injured, and a number of firearms and ammunition were found in the suspects' possession after their arrest.

"Terrorism has no place among us," the directorate said, adding that the suspects had met their "just fate".

The Public Security Directorate did not identify the suspects' affiliation or say whether they belonged to any militant group.

Jordanian authorities have said the attack was carried out by "extremist terrorists", but it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan.

There has been no claim of responsibility.

Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya on Monday said authorities were reviewing the circumstances that led young people towards extremism and would hold accountable anyone found to have participated in the attack.

King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against Islamist militant groups, has ordered security forces to respond with an "iron fist" to the rare attack on Jordan's Christian minority.

Such violence is highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though authorities say they have foiled several Islamist militant plots over the years. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Ex-Japan prime minister Yasuo Fukuda dies
articles.excerpt: Former Japanese prime minister Yasuo Fukuda, who used his brief period in office to seek closer ties with Asian neighbours…
articles.fullText:
Former Japanese prime minister Yasuo Fukuda, who used his brief period in office to seek closer ties with Asian neighbours, particularly China, has died at the age of 90, the Nikkei business daily reported on Monday.

Beijing expressed condolences over his passing.

The Japanese politician, the first son of a prime minister to become premier himself, died on Thursday from heart failure, the Nikkei said.

Becoming prime minister on the sudden resignation of Shinzo Abe in 2007, Fukuda lasted less than a year – a tenure even shorter than his father Takeo's two-year stint.

A graduate in economics from Tokyo's prestigious Waseda University, Fukuda spent nearly two decades working his way up the ranks of an oil company – including a two-year posting in the United States – before resigning to become a political secretary when his father became premier in 1976.

Elected to Japan's more powerful lower house of parliament in 1990, Fukuda was chief cabinet secretary from 2000 to 2004, resigning as one of several cabinet ministers to admit not paying into the pension system.

Known for his testy manner, the bespectacled Fukuda drew criticism in 2003 for off-the-record comments in which he suggested women who dressed provocatively were asking to be raped.

When Fukuda succeeded Abe he joked he might have drawn the short straw in assuming office given the divided parliament and opposition parties' ability to delay legislation.

Frustrated with the stalled legislative process, Fukuda resigned in 2008, the second of six prime ministers to quit after only around a year in office.

Known as a diplomatic dove, Fukuda made several visits to China after leaving office in an effort to improve often fraught relations.

Speaking at a regular briefing on Monday, Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun called Fukuda an old friend of the Chinese people who held the "correct view" of history.

Guo praised him for making significant contributions to the development of bilateral relations, citing the China-Japan Joint Statement on All-round Promotion of Strategic Relationship of Mutual Benefit that was issued in 2008 when he was prime minister.

Fukuda leaves a son, Tatsuo, who is also a lawmaker and has been viewed as a potential future prime minister. (Reuters/RTHK)
_____________________________
Last updated: 2026-10-26 HKT 16:54

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Xi opens Party plenum on governance
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping opened the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC)…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping opened the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in Beijing on Monday.

Xi, who is also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a work report on behalf of the Politburo and explained a draft decision by the Central Committee on major issues concerning strengthening Party self-governance.

The draft decision summarises the achievements and experience of full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era in a truth-seeking manner, and offers in-depth analysis of the situation and tasks concerning Party building at present and for the future.

It also sets out strategic plans for strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance, according to a Politburo meeting in September that submitted the document to the plenum for review.

The plenary session will last till Thursday.

The fifth plenum comes ahead of a major Party congress next year, where Xi is expected to oversee a leadership reshuffle.

State media published an article ahead of the gathering, based on a speech Xi gave in January in which he railed against "two-faced" officials who appear to comply with central directives but "inwardly resist", pursue "individualism" and are "politically opportunistic". (Xinhua/AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Full MPF portability 'can help drive down fees'
articles.excerpt: Lawmakers hailed on Monday an upcoming arrangement that allows employees to transfer not only their own mandatory provident fund contributions…
articles.fullText:
Lawmakers hailed on Monday an upcoming arrangement that allows employees to transfer not only their own mandatory provident fund contributions but also their employer’s to a scheme of their choice once every calendar year.

Their remarks came as phase one of the MPF Full Portability scheme – which grants employees greater autonomy by allowing them to transfer accrued mandatory contributions by their employers to a scheme of their choice – is set to begin on December 21.

Speaking on a RTHK radio programme, lawmaker Chau Siu-chung said he supported the arrangement as workers would be able to choose the MPF trustee they considered to be the best for them as well as foster more competition and help drive down administrative fees.

He also said that the current eMPF platform would make the transfer process simpler and easier.

Chau, also a non-executive director of the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority, noted that many workers remained unclear about what MPF “full portability” means and that public awareness in this regard needed to be strengthened.

“I think public awareness right now is indeed not ideal – about 80 percent of people are basically not very clear about what full portability means, there is definitely a need to do more,” he said.

Chau also called on the public to be alert to unfair sales practices.

He urged the government to take this opportunity to summarise and simplify information about different trustees so that workers could have clear, easy-to-compare information to take reference from.

Speaking on RTHK’s Backchat programme, lawmaker Lam Chun-sing also welcomed the arrangement but noted that employees should avoid changing their scheme frequently as it may cause high administrative costs and may affect their returns.

“MPF investment is a long-term investment for retirement [so] that we want to achieve stable growth of the MPF contributions instead of short-term returns like share investment or other investment tools,” he said.

“If you frequently change your scheme or transfer your MPF contribution to different trustees, this may cause high administrative costs and may affect your return.”

Lam also encouraged workers who are not investment professionals or do not have time to manage their scheme to consider using the default investment strategy, saying it automatically reduces risks and uses a diversified investment approach to bring favourable returns.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Saudi alliance 'turns to Iran amid Houthi attacks'
articles.excerpt: Top officials from the Mecca Pact countries Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan are set to meet Iranian officials in Tehran…
articles.fullText:
Top officials from the Mecca Pact countries Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan are set to meet Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday to discuss regional coordination, two people with knowledge of the matter said.

Saudi Arabia will be represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, and Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, the people said on condition of anonymity.

The Turkish head of intelligence would also join, one of the people said.

The Saudi government media office and Pakistan's military media wing did not respond to requests for comment.

The planned talks would be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia has come under escalating attacks from Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis.

Saudi Arabia intercepted another wave of missiles and drones on Sunday as fighting with the militant group continued unabated.

Ministers from the Mecca Pact countries held an emergency meeting in Riyadh this month and agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.

The conflict has become an increasingly destabilising element in the US-Israeli offensive against Iran, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point ⁠in the wider war.

Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

The agreement's first article says the parties shall use "all necessary means" to eliminate threats to one another's territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognised borders.

Efforts by the Turkish parliament to ratify the agreement began last week and are still underway, while Pakistan approved the pact last week. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Man bitten by dog in Yuen Long
articles.excerpt: A 26-year-old man was bitten by a dog in Yuen Long on Monday and taken to Pok Oi Hospital for…
articles.fullText:
A 26-year-old man was bitten by a dog in Yuen Long on Monday and taken to Pok Oi Hospital for treatment.

The incident happened at around 8am near a warehouse on Kam Pok Road.

Reports say he was chased by three dogs, one of which bit his leg.

The dog has been taken away by the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department for examination.

In a statement published late on Monday, the AFCD said the captured dog is a microchipped mixed breed with a valid licence.

The incident came just over a month after a 27-year-old woman was found dead on Pok Wai South Road, with multiple animal bite wounds on her body.
_____________________________
Last updated: 2026-10-26 HKT 21:41

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK can assist green push within the Belt and Road: CE
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee on Monday said Hong Kong could help enhance connections among Belt and Road economies and combine…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee on Monday said Hong Kong could help enhance connections among Belt and Road economies and combine their strengths to advance the development of green technologies and sustainable businesses.

Lee made the remarks at the Belt and Road Green Innovation Conference, which is being held in the SAR for the first time.

He said Hong Kong, as a leading green and sustainable finance hub, connects green projects with global capital.

“For example, a solar energy project can bring together Chinese mainland equipment suppliers, a Southeast Asian developer and Middle Eastern investors,” Lee said.

“Hong Kong can help these partners raise finance, structure their investments, arrange insurance and manage cross-border risks.

“Our contribution, let me add, is about more than matching capital with projects. Hong Kong’s professional services also help ensure that a project is bankable and insurable.”

Lee said Hong Kong is also able to connect green technologies with the markets that need them.

He said the SAR would launch a Green Technology Bridgehead Programme next year, which could help mainland and overseas green enterprises spread their ideas and take their solutions to Belt and Road markets.

The city, meanwhile, could also assist firms from Belt and Road countries reach out to the wider world, he added.

Lee went on to say that the SAR could provide Belt and Road partners with financing, project management and risk management services for green infrastructure and sustainable development projects.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK rises as region slips ahead of key tech earnings
articles.excerpt: Asian stocks slipped on Monday as the dour mood that sullied last week's trading continued, with investors gearing up for…
articles.fullText:
Asian stocks slipped on Monday as the dour mood that sullied last week's trading continued, with investors gearing up for a crucial run of central bank decisions and tech earnings.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened up 63 points, or 0.28 percent, at 23,156.

The tech index was up 16 points, or 0.43 percent, to 3,888 while the China enterprises index rose 21 points, or 0.28 percent, to 7,777.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index opened down 19 points, or 0.53 percent, at 3,671.

The Shenzhen Component Index fell 113 points, or 0.97 percent, to 11,560 while the ChiNext Index was 38 points, or 1.43 percent, lower at 2,645.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 243 points, or 0.39 percent, lower at 62,449, peaked in morning trading at 62,856 before being 188 points down at one stage before lunch.

In Seoul, the Kospi fell 51 points, or 0.92 percent, to open at 5,499 and was 54 points lower at one stage before noon.

AI-linked firms continued to struggle amid worries about the sustainability of the colossal investment boom that pushed stock markets to multiple record highs in the first half of the year.

Traders are growing increasingly worried about when the vast sums pumped into the sector will see returns, if any, while rising interest rates and bond yields are now calling companies' finances into question.

This week sees the release of earnings from US titans and Magnificent Seven members Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet as well as South Korean chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung.

Results from Tesla and Meta last week further stoked spending worries and helped drag stocks lower.

"The AI complex remains under a microscope ahead of what may be the most important stretch of earnings season so far," said SPI Asset Management's Stephen Innes.

"Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon are about to walk on stage, and this is not one of those quarters where a company can simply beat the number, raise the guidance by a whisker and expect applause. Investors want proof now.

"They want to know whether the billions going into the compute buildout are building a durable earnings machine or just a shinier version of the same old capex furnace."

Also in view this week are policy decisions by the US Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan.

While the Fed is expected to hold borrowing costs, traders will be keen to get an insight into its thinking following last month's hike and as inflation remains well above its two percent target. (AFP/Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: First int'l flight takes off from Sydney's new airport
articles.excerpt: The first international flight took off on Monday from a new, multi-billion-dollar airport in the fast-growing western suburbs of Sydney…
articles.fullText:
The first international flight took off on Monday from a new, multi-billion-dollar airport in the fast-growing western suburbs of Sydney.

After more than four decades of planning, Western Sydney International Airport offers the first alternative to the city's main airport, which has been operating for more than a century.

An Air New Zealand plane from Auckland landed and soon afterwards flew out of the airport in the morning, launching a three-flights-a-week service to Sydney's largely working-class western suburbs.

"It's not every day you get to be part of opening a brand-new international airport," said Air New Zealand chief operations officer Kate Boyer.

"Western Sydney is home to more than 2.5 million people and it's a further gateway for Australian visitors to discover everything our country has to offer."

The new single-runway airport, Australia's first new major aviation hub in more than five decades, began domestic flights on Sunday, and freight operations in July.

Sydney's main airport, Kingsford Smith, is Australia's busiest, its three runways handling more than 42 million passengers last year.

Lying in Botany Bay just nine kilometres from the city centre, planes using the airport roar over many city homes, and a curfew bars passenger aircraft from operating during the night.

The new airport in western Sydney has no such restrictions.

"Through our 24-hour operations, Western Sydney International Airport gives airlines greater flexibility to connect into global hubs and travellers more choice in how they reach the world," said airport chief executive Simon Hickey.

Qantas' budget carrier Jetstar is now the main domestic carrier, flying to the Gold Coast, Melbourne and Brisbane.

The airport says other international carriers are coming, including Qatar Airways from December 2027, Fiji Airways from March 2027, and Vietjet Air from January 2027.

Built at a cost of A$5.3 billion (US$3.7 billion), excluding surrounding transport works, the airport is reachable by road, but is not expected to have a direct rail link until at least December 2027.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the new airport marked a "wonderful new chapter" for Australia.

It would also drive jobs into western Sydney, an area often overshadowed by the city's famed harbour and central business district (CBD), he said.

"For too long, Sydney has looked towards the harbour and the CBD. What this does is turn it around to where people live, to where jobs occur, to where investment occurs in western Sydney."

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Doncic erupts for 52 as Lakers maintain perfect start
articles.excerpt: Luka Doncic scored a monster 52 points as the Los Angeles Lakers maintained their perfect start to life after LeBron…
articles.fullText:
Luka Doncic scored a monster 52 points as the Los Angeles Lakers maintained their perfect start to life after LeBron James with a 132-123 win over the Utah Jazz.

Now the undisputed superstar of the Lakers since James departed this summer for Philadelphia, Doncic also provided 10 assists and eight rebounds in a masterful performance, with eight three-pointers and two steals.

Doncic was supported by Austin Reaves, who had 29 points, as the visitors pulled decisively clear in the last four minutes of a game they had trailed for long periods.

"It's one of the best feelings... down the stretch, tight game, hitting those threes," said Doncic.

"Played the basketball we know how to play. We are learning our lesson...we cannot start games like this any more."

It was the first 50-point game by an NBA player this season. Slovenian point guard Doncic was the league's top scorer last season.

After cruising to comfortable opening wins against the Golden State Warriors and city rival Clippers, the Lakers overcame their first real adversity of the nascent season in Salt Lake City.

Utah led nearly the entire first half, pulling as many as 18 points clear, with Finland's Lauri Markkanen on scintillating form.

But the Lakers rallied. A Doncic three-point pull-up shot with seconds remaining in the second quarter gave Los Angeles a slender lead at the interval.

The Jazz had inched back in front with just over four minutes remaining, when another Doncic trey tied up the score 116-116.

From there Doncic and Reaves were relentless, outscoring the entire Jazz offence in the final quarter between them, as the new-look Lakers moved to a perfect 3-0 start.

"We have a tight group. I think everybody new that came, they feel very welcome here. That's what we want," said Doncic. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Medical products regulator 'aims to boost innovation'
articles.excerpt: A new regulatory authority for medical products in Hong Kong aims to gain international trust and serve patients around the…
articles.fullText:
A new regulatory authority for medical products in Hong Kong aims to gain international trust and serve patients around the world, according to its controller Li Zili.

The Hong Kong Centre for Medical Products Regulation, which will be established in the SAR by the end of the year, is expected to promote the “primary evaluation” of drugs and medical devices to speed up their clinical application.

Speaking to reporters, Li said the centre’s mission is to protect public health and promote medical innovation.

“We need to build a medical products regulatory authority with comprehensive capabilities – one that is trusted internationally,” he said.

“We should leverage our unique strategic position in medical products regulation – we not only serve patients in Hong Kong, but also keep the world in mind and serve all patients around the world.”

Li said the “primary evaluation” to be established in the future should complement the existing framework and enhance the international community’s trust in the centre through a scientific and transparent regulatory system.

He added the centre would not only become a super connector linking the mainland and the world, but also boost medical reforms and innovations.

Li went on to say that authorities would set up an interdisciplinary scientific team that focuses on clinical review with the aim of accelerating international cooperation.

Meanwhile, Director of Health Ronald Lam said Li possesses practical experience in regulatory affairs and public health and is familiar with international medical products policies.

Lam expressed confidence that Li would be able to reform the system with his experience and leadership skills.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: 'US Marine indicted on murder charge in Okinawa'
articles.excerpt: Japanese prosecutors have indicted a US Marine on suspicion of murdering a woman in Okinawa, reports said on Monday. The…
articles.fullText:
Japanese prosecutors have indicted a US Marine on suspicion of murdering a woman in Okinawa, reports said on Monday.

The case has prompted public outrage, caused Japan's premier to slam the "heinous crime" and reignited controversy over the heavy US military presence on the southern island.

According to the indictment document, the 20-year-old suspect allegedly strangled a 39-year-old woman from Naha in a hotel with a telephone cord on October 3, the Yomiuri Shimbun reported.

He is also accused of stealing a backpack containing the woman's wallet and other belongings, the newspaper said, and has been indicted on robbery charges.

The Marine denied the allegations at the time of his arrest but has now made statements that imply some involvement in the case, the Yomiuri and other media said, citing investigative sources.

Prosecutors were not immediately reachable when contacted by AFP.

Crimes including rapes, assaults, hit-and-runs and drunk driving by US military personnel have long triggered protests on the southern Japanese island, which has for years urged other regions in the country to share the burden of hosting US troops. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Lula re-elected Brazil leader in comeback win
articles.excerpt: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won an unprecedented fourth term on Sunday, the country's electoral court said, in…
articles.fullText:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won an unprecedented fourth term on Sunday, the country's electoral court said, in a shock result that defied polls, precedent and global anti-incumbent sentiment to put the brakes on a wave of right-wing election victories across Latin America.

Lula, an icon of the global left and the most dominant force in Brazilian politics this century, defeated Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. The senator had finished first in the election's first round and hoped to revive his father's far-right movement.

At times, Lula's reelection looked like a long shot, as voters soured on him and his Workers' Party after years of corruption scandals and rising prices, while sweeping societal changes left the former metalworker and union leader looking out of touch with an increasingly app-based economy and its growing ranks of informal workers.

Lula's victory marks another comeback in a career full of them. The 80-year-old was jailed from 2018 to 2019 on corruption charges that were later overturned, paving the way for him to beat Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election.

"He is a statesman, a giant," leftist federal lawmaker Erika Hilton, who was with Lula in Sao Paulo during the vote count, told Reuters.

Pollsters said better-than-expected turnout had powered Lula to victory. Leonardo Barreto, the co-founder of consultancy Think Policy, said voters had chosen Lula's familiar embrace over Bolsonaro's novelty.

"People today are choosing between change, with some apprehension, and a known path, which guarantees certain rights," he said.

During the campaign, Lula pointed to a track record of falling poverty and inequality, while unemployment, illiteracy and deforestation hit record lows during his third term.

He warned Bolsonaro would cut welfare spending, backslide on social advances and hand over Brazil's sovereignty to US President Donald Trump, whose State Department led a campaign to get the Bolsonaros back to power.

Lula's win deprives Trump of a major addition to what has been a growing bloc of friendly right-wing Latin American governments that have embraced Washington's agenda on security and migration.

Celso Amorim, a former Lula foreign minister, told Reuters the leftist "would be very important for establishing a point of balance in Latin America. Lula is that balance."

Lula becomes the first candidate since Brazil's return to democracy in the 1980s to be elected after finishing second in the first round.

Lula, who was president between 2003 and 2011, campaigned on a potent mix of pragmatism and populism that has shaped his career in national politics for half a century, rolling out a slew of reforms aimed at improving the lives of workers and poor Brazilians.

These gained steam with late-campaign pledges that ranged from free nationwide weekend public transport, which has to be formally submitted to Congress, to a 15 percent increase in his trademark welfare program that is already being implemented.

Lula also championed a constitutional amendment that became Brazil's biggest labour reform in decades, which passed with wide support in Congress.

Still, Lula's fourth term could be his most difficult yet, after Brazil elected its most conservative Congress since returning to democracy in the 1980s.

Combined, Bolsonaro's Liberal Party (PL) and allied parties could control over 280 seats in the lower house and up to 50 seats in the Senate, enough for comfortable majorities in both chambers.

"He is likely to be a lame duck from the start," said Oliver Stuenkel, a professor of international relations at the Getulio Vargas Foundation in São Paulo.

The incoming legislature will likely deepen recent trends of presidents ceding power to Congress, Stuenkel said, predicting Lula will face waning influence over Supreme Court nominations, unwieldy party coalitions, and even the threat of impeachment.

Lula faces an economy that his government forecasts will grow a meager 2.3 percent next year, adding to fiscal concerns tied to high interest rates and public debt that has risen past 82 percent of GDP, the highest since the pandemic.

The president's critics blame spending, though interest costs have driven most of the increase in debt. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Nigeria widens hunt for possible Ebola cases
articles.excerpt: Nigeria has widened a hunt for potential Ebola cases, with an additional nine contacts traced, health authorities said on Sunday…
articles.fullText:
Nigeria has widened a hunt for potential Ebola cases, with an additional nine contacts traced, health authorities said on Sunday.

"As of now, we have 53 primary contacts," said Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) boss Jide Idris.

The count was up from 44 people who had come in contact with a woman who fell ill with Ebola in the Nigerian capital Abuja.

The woman, the 42-year-old wife of a Swiss embassy staff worker based in Abuja, had been travelling in Uganda with her husband before returning to Nigeria. She is receiving treatment and remains the only confirmed case.

A test on a suspected case, in Rivers State, in the Niger Delta, came back negative, Idris told reporters.

The initial 44 contacts were health care workers, while the additional nine comprise more health staff as well as members of the infected woman's family and household staff, Idris said.

The World Health Organization has warned that Africa is facing a "complex" Ebola outbreak with the virus now present in west, east and central Africa.

Health authorities in Nigeria successfully stemmed a previous Ebola outbreak a decade ago but some experts are worried about how much the illness could have spread in the time between the woman's arrival – October 3 – and her diagnosis, announced on Tuesday.

Nigerian authorities have announced enhanced screenings for international airport arrivals.

Nigeria last week announced west Africa's first case from an outbreak ravaging Democratic Republic of the Congo – an imported case of the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no vaccine or specific treatment.

The DRC has recorded more than 4,600 deaths since it declared its 17th Ebola outbreak in May.

Uganda has had 20 cases, including two deaths, on its territory but the World Health Organization officially declared it Ebola-free. Almost all the cases were people who had visited DRC.

Uganda said on Sunday its nationals returning from DRC would have to spend 21 days in quarantine.

Ebola is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe haemorrhagic fever.

Kenya has reported two deaths this month.

The country had not reported a single case until a Kenyan man who had been living in DRC died after returning home. The second death was a close contact of the man, authorities said. As of Friday the country had seven Ebola cases in isolation. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Antonelli on brink of title with US Grand Prix victory
articles.excerpt: Kimi Antonelli moved to within striking distance of his first world championship title as he powered to an emphatic victory…
articles.fullText:
Kimi Antonelli moved to within striking distance of his first world championship title as he powered to an emphatic victory at the US Grand Prix in Austin on Sunday.

It was his ninth win of the season and with his only rivals Mercedes teammate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finishing eighth and fourth respectively, the 20-year-old Italian needs just to come in ninth in next week's race in Mexico to become the youngest ever Formula One champion.

He is also set to become the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

Antonelli finished over 13 seconds ahead of the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc with Red Bull's Max Verstappen completing the podium.

Antonelli started the race in pole position and after a clean start already had a 2sec lead by the end of the opening lap, at which point the result never seemed in doubt, mechanical failure and pit stop disasters notwithstanding.

Verstappen was beaten off the start by Leclerc, who started in third, but the four-time world champion wasted no time in reclaiming second spot. Leclerc, however, overtook him in the latter part of the race and Verstappen was left hanging on for third as Hamilton also closed.

Antonelli would have become the youngest ever champion, smashing the current record of Sebastian Vettel who was 23 years and 133 days when he won his fist title in 2010, if Russell had finished lower than eighth and Hamilton failed to make the top four.

Russell, who has had some terrible luck all season, was hit with a 5sec penalty for running off the track on the opening lap and struggled to get past McLaren's Oscar Piastri who came in seventh.

Lando Norris, the outgoing champion, was running second until the closing laps when his tyres appeared to give up and he had to settle for fifth with Isack Hadjar sixth in the second Red Bull. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Mbappe double helps Real down Barca in Clasico
articles.excerpt: Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on…
articles.fullText:
Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points.

French superstar Mbappe opened the scoring before the interval and then slotted home late on to inflict Barca's first domestic defeat of the campaign after Raphinha had equalised for the champions.

Real Madrid remain third, behind Atletico Madrid and Hansi Flick's Barca, who had won their first nine games before a chastening week.

The Catalans suffered a second straight defeat after losing on Tuesday against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.

Mourinho was delighted with his team's display in his first Clasico back at the helm of Madrid.

"My team had an extraordinary game, very organised, good concentration, with courage to play out from the back against a team that presses you a lot," Mourinho told reporters.

"We had chances for the second goal... obviously Barca had a strong reaction but we were calm and organised and at 1-1 we never lost our tranquility."

Barca had won six of the seven previous Clasicos since Flick arrived but were surprisingly subdued against Mourinho's side.

"In general we didn't have a great game, in the first half we weren't ourselves, there were a lot of things we could have done better," Barcelona midfielder Pedri told DAZN.

"We wanted to win the Clasico in front of our fans, but the season is very long... a league is not won here."

Los Blancos, without suspended winger Vinicius Junior, won their fifth straight game across all competitions and are finding their footing under veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho.

After two trophyless seasons Madrid turned back to Mourinho to try and stop Barca's dominance, and this result will give them hope they are on the right track.

The opening period of the game was cagey, with few opportunities.

Barca defender Pau Cubarsi twice reacted well to shut down Mbappe, while Real Madrid's Marc Cucurella took a rapid liking for Lamine Yamal's shirt, constantly grabbing at the 19-year-old winger.

Anthony Gordon, playing in his first Clasico since joining Barcelona from Newcastle, backheeled the ball to Raphinha, who fired narrowly wide as Barca threatened.

The hosts were dealt a setback when young defender Xavi Espart pulled up hurt and needed to be replaced by Alejandro Balde before the half-hour mark.

Andriy Lunin, playing in goal for Madrid after Thibaut Courtois pulled out of the squad with flu, saved at his near post from Gordon before the visitors took the lead.

Mbappe scored his 10th league goal of the season and also his easiest, with Barca's Gerard Martin clearing a cross straight at the Frenchman, who deflected it into the net.

Barca responded by carving out a glorious chance for an equaliser but teenage sensation Yamal for once miscued in front of goal, firing wide when poised to level.

The game opened up and Yan Diomande came close to doubling Madrid's lead before half-time, drilling into the side-netting.

Martin redeemed himself early in the second half as he held off Jude Bellingham, who could neither beat the defender nor find a free Mbappe.

Raphinha, who had a quiet first half, pulled Barcelona level just after the hour mark.

Pedri fed the Brazilian, La Liga's top goalscorer with 13, who fired through Bellingham's legs and Lunin could not keep the shot out.

The Ukrainian goalkeeper did make a superb save to deny Martin at a corner, as Barcelona flowed forward with the wind finally in their sails.

Yamal bent an effort wide with Lunin at full stretch and Barca substitute Frenkie de Jong had a shot desperately blocked by Dean Huijsen.

There was a sting in the tail for the Catalans though as substitute Gabriel Jesus lost possession and Madrid raced through on goal.

Eduardo Camavinga beat Cubarsi and unselfishly cut the ball back for Mbappe to tuck home his second of the night into an empty net with Joan Garcia drawn out of position.

It brought up a century of goals since Mbappe joined Madrid from PSG in 2024, although the trophies to match have not yet followed. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Man United lose again as Liverpool climb to fourth
articles.excerpt: Michael Carrick was pushed to the brink of being sacked after Manchester United slumped to a miserable 3-0 home defeat…
articles.fullText:
Michael Carrick was pushed to the brink of being sacked after Manchester United slumped to a miserable 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth, while Alexander Isak extended his hot streak in Liverpool's 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday.

Carrick's bold decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes backfired as defeat stretched United's winless run to eight games and left them 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone.

For the third time in four seasons, the Cherries won by a three-goal margin at Old Trafford as strikes from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson secured a fully deserved victory for Marco Rose's side.

Fernandes was critical of Carrick's tactics in a 4-1 Champions League thrashing at Como on Wednesday.

The United boss said the decision to leave out last season's Premier League Player of the Year was a "purely football" driven, but it was hard to believe Fernandes was not being punished as he was left on the bench for the entire match.

Carrick was taunted with chants of "you're getting sacked in the morning" from the Bournemouth fans.

But on this evidence, dismissing another manager is far from a quick fix for a club that has fallen dramatically from grace since Alex Ferguson's retirement after winning their most recent English title 13 years ago.

A strong finish to last season during Carrick's interim spell in charge secured third place in the Premier League.

Yet with just one win against promoted Ipswich, United have taken just seven points from eight league games so far this season – their lowest tally at this stage of a season since 1986-87.

United's players were booed off by the few frustrated fans that remained inside Old Trafford at the end of their heaviest home defeat since 2024.

United's co-owners the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe were also targeted for angry chants, although Carrick largely avoided the fans' ire.

It is unlikely that sympathy vote will spare the former United midfielder from the axe.

At Anfield, Liverpool struck twice in quick succession in the first half, with Pascal Gross's own goal followed by Isak's latest strike.

Isak has netted six times in seven league games this season and has three goals in his last four matches.

After a turbulent debut season following his acrimonious move from Newcastle, the Sweden striker is finally beginning to repay his £125 million fee.

It was a welcome first taste of top-flight success at Anfield for Reds boss Andoni Iraola, who had failed to win his first three league games on Merseyside since arriving from Bournemouth in the close season.

The Spaniard, who had won Champions League and League Cup games at Anfield, has led Liverpool to four successive victories in all competitions since the chastening 3-0 home defeat against Manchester City.

Liverpool have climbed to fourth place, just one point behind third-placed Brighton after inflicting the high-flying Seagulls' second league loss this term.

The rampant Reds are six points behind leaders City as they eye a potential title challenge.

William Osula and Harvey Barnes scored in the second half as Newcastle piled pressure on Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage with a 2-0 win at Selhurst Park.

Thrashed 5-0 at rivals Brighton last weekend, 17th-placed Palace have won just twice in eight league games under Sage, who arrived from Lens in the close season to replace Oliver Glasner.

Hull's unbeaten home record remains intact but the Tigers have not tasted victory for seven games after a 1-1 draw with Brentford at the MKM Stadium.

Oli McBurnie's 24th-minute penalty, awarded when Aaron Hickey fouled Tim Iroegbunam, put Hull ahead, but Dango Ouattara equalised in the 63rd minute.

Elsewhere on the pitch, Sunderland hosted Leeds to a 0-0 draw. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: 'US fully resumes missile warnings for Ukraine'
articles.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said US warnings about imminent Russian ballistic missile strikes, critical to Ukraine's air defences, had been…
articles.fullText:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said US warnings about imminent Russian ballistic missile strikes, critical to Ukraine's air defences, had been fully restored after recent issues.

Speaking to Ukraine's TSN television channel, he said SpaceX's Starshield satellite internet had been working at speeds of up to 420 kilometres per hour since early on Saturday morning, after it had been throttled earlier in October amid diplomatic pressure on Kyiv from Washington.

Zelensky said he discussed both issues in a meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, casting the changes as results of that meeting.

The US has pressed Ukraine to suspend strikes on Russian oil refineries, which it argues added to high energy prices, a sensitive issue for the Trump administration amid its war on Iran and US midterm elections next month.

Zelensky said that in order for Kyiv to halt the strikes, Moscow must stop hitting Ukraine's power infrastructure, or the US should allow the use of Starshield over Russia to detect launch places of its ballistic missiles, or supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles.

Speaking about the upcoming technical talks between Kyiv, Moscow and Washington in November, Zelensky said Ukraine would not discuss limits to its armed forces, or enforced post-war neutrality. Kyiv has long sought entry into Nato despite the reticence of some members.

Zelensky also renewed his push for a trilateral US-brokered meeting between him and Vladimir Putin.

The Ukrainian leader has long argued Putin is the only person in Russia who can make major decisions to end the war or meaningfully discuss core issues, such as the fate of the nearly 20 percent of Ukraine that Russia occupies.

"The issue of territories is a red line that can be discussed exclusively at the level of leaders," Zelensky said. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: France's Le Pen launches presidential bid
articles.excerpt: Marine Le Pen, France's far-right candidate to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, kicked off her campaign on Sunday vowing to "restore…
articles.fullText:
Marine Le Pen, France's far-right candidate to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, kicked off her campaign on Sunday vowing to "restore the rule of law" if elected next year.

Le Pen – the frontrunner in the polls – seems to be benefiting from the convulsions France has been going through for weeks, which has seen violence flare on the sidelines of mass cost-of-living rallies.

"We are going to restore the rule of law," she said, after looting and arson erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations last weekend.

She was addressing 8,500 supporters of her nationalist, anti-immigration party in the city of Orleans, where Joan of Arc – revered by the far right as a symbol of national resistance – lifted an English siege in 1429.

"We are proposing for the country not a return to the past, but the dawn of a new era," the 58-year-old told the crowd, which broke into chants of "We're going to win, we're going to win."

Le Pen vowed to preserve France's cultural identity, from its language and traditions to its values and way of life, drawing thunderous cheers from supporters waving French flags.

"We want France to regain its strength," she added.

Supporter Charlene Malingre, wearing a scarf emblazoned with the words "Marine President", said she was increasingly concerned about insecurity in France.

"I think Marine Le Pen could save France from the state it's in today... particularly when it comes to the economy, security and maintaining law and order," the 23-year-old told AFP.

More than 400,000 people marched in major French cities on Saturday to protest against the rising cost of living. Clashes erupted after groups of masked protesters broke away from the demonstrations.

Police made more than 1,300 arrests and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez blamed much of the violence on "ultra-left" extremists.

Similar nationwide protests a week earlier also descended into unrest, following four weeks of student demonstrations over the poor state of France's schools.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu will hold talks with high school student organisations on Monday, a leader of one of the groups told AFP.

"We hope the prime minister will satisfy out demands," said Louis Letoublon, a leader of Les Lyceens!.

The unions and Yellow Vest protesters have vowed to keep up their street marches in the weeks ahead.

Le Pen addressed supporters of her far-right party after deciding to run in elections beginning in April, despite an appeals court upholding a graft conviction against her.

She has accused Macron's centrist government of being soft on violent protesters and lacking authority.

"Who can claim that there is a rule of law when hordes come to ransack and burn our buildings?" she said.

The anti-immigration party's veteran candidate, who has run for the presidency three times already, also promised tougher immigration laws.

"We will restore our borders, and even establish double borders, both French and European," she said.

"French nationality will once again become a privilege that is either inherited or earned," she said.

On Sunday, police were filtering traffic going into Orleans, after thousands of counter-protesters opposed to Le Pen and her anti-immigration, nationalist RN marched in the city on Saturday chanting anti-fascist slogans.

"If the far right comes to power, we fear things will become much worse," 35-year-old yoga teacher Antonine Rochet said on Saturday.

If Le Pen wins the two-stage presidential elections in April and May, she has vowed to cut the cost of living through capped household energy bills, reduced taxes and trimming France's contribution to the European Union.

French voters, angry over Macron's perceived detachment over his two terms and his recent orders to curb the protests, are turning to more extremist politics, polling suggests.

An Ipsos survey published Saturday suggested Le Pen would win 32-34 percent of first-round votes.

The poll also found widespread anger over the unrest, with a majority believing that the government bears responsibility. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Netanyahu warns Iran may try to disrupt election
articles.excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said Iran and its allies might try to disrupt Tuesday's elections in his country…
articles.fullText:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said Iran and its allies might try to disrupt Tuesday's elections in his country, as he warned the Islamic republic against any hostile acts.

The remarks came as Israel's Channel 12 reported, citing unnamed sources, that there had been a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the premier denied.

Netanyahu has campaigned heavily on his security credentials, touting the war he launched against Iran in February alongside the United States and suggesting that he alone can see it through.

"We have intelligence signs that our enemies, Iran and its proxies, could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections," Netanyahu said in a video released by his office on Sunday.

"Don't test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows," he added, noting the military was ready for both defensive and offensive operations.

In its report on the purported confrontation between Netanyahu and Zamir, Channel 12 said the latter had "demanded an in-depth discussion before carrying out the directive he had received, as well as legal guarantees and the signatures of the political echelon".

It did not offer details of the directive, but cited sources saying there were concerns within the army that the war might be exploited for political gain.

In a television appearance later in the day, Netanyahu dismissed the report as "nothing but rubbish".

Opposition leader Yair Lapid referenced the report in a post on X, accusing Netanyahu of seeking to put off the vote.

"Tonight it was published that he wants to set off an escalation and a confrontation with Iran, just to postpone the elections," he said.

"This man has lost his grip. We absolutely must send him home."

Earlier on Sunday, the premier posted an AI-generated image of a mushroom cloud engulfing Tel Aviv, alongside text attributed to a right-wing political commentator calling Iran an existential threat and arguing that all the other issues discussed this election season were trivial in comparison.

On Wednesday, Netanyahu said he had sent a directive to Israel's security forces to topple Iran's clerical state.

A day earlier, he posted a video of himself in front of a fighter jet speaking to US President Donald Trump by phone saying they would "finish the job" together. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Opposition leader Machado returns to Venezuela
articles.excerpt: Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner Maria Corina Machado returned to her home country Sunday after almost a…
articles.fullText:
Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner Maria Corina Machado returned to her home country Sunday after almost a year in exile, greeting ecstatic supporters at a church in the city of Barquisimeto.

"I am here. With you," Machado announced in Spanish on X.

Video shared by her Vente party showed the leader, in a trademark white tee-shirt and blue jeans, embracing cheering supporters at a church. "Venezuela will be free!" the party said.

Machado's return is likely to heap pressure on interim president Delcy Rodriguez, who has led the country under Washington's watchful eye since US forces ousted longtime leader Nicolas Maduro in January.

A close ally of Machado, exiled opposition candidate Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia, reposted her message and said: "Venezuela! I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear Maria Corina, is on Venezuelan soil."

"Very soon I will be with you all and her so that our country can truly advance toward freedom," he added.

Gonzalez Urrutia stood against Maduro in the 2024 presidential election after Machado was ruled ineligible.

Venezuelan authorities declared Maduro the winner but never shared detailed results, while a tally released by the opposition showed Gonzalez Urrutia winning easily.

Machado, 59, has been in exile since covertly leaving her South American homeland in late 2025 to receive her Nobel Peace Prize.

While based in Panama, she has tried at least seven times to return but has been blocked by Venezuelan authorities, according to her party.

The month after she fled Venezuela, US forces seized Maduro in a stunning nighttime raid and flew him to New York to face criminal charges.

Machado has repeatedly praised President Donald Trump for launching the risky operation, and even gifted him the Nobel medal she received.

Asked by reporters Sunday about Machado's return, Trump said "I don't know anything about it, but I think she's a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel prize, so how can I say anything else?"

"I hope she's safe. She's a very nice woman. But we're doing very well in Venezuela," he added.

Trump has repeatedly expressed satisfaction with Rodriguez – who was Maduro's deputy – as she has acceded to US demands, particularly on granting access to Venezuelan oil.

Rodriguez and her brother, who leads Venezuela's legislature, pushed through reforms to the Venezuelan oil industry and passed an amnesty law earlier this year.

The interim government has held multiple rounds of negotiations with a faction of the opposition, which has led to an agreement to reform the judiciary but not yet set a date for new elections.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Machado's return had been made possible by the Washington-backed talks – and he urged her to support them going forward.

"We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy," he said.

Machado has been sidelined from the discussions, but the opposition delegation welcomed her return "in freedom."

Last week, thousands demonstrated in Caracas and other cities, demanding her return, carrying signs that read "Elections NOW and this time they're not going to steal from us" and "Brave MCM," referring to Machado's initials.

Her Vente Venezuela party has demanded elections next year and the lifting of the political disqualification that prevented her from running in the last presidential vote. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Houthis launch new attack on Riyadh airport
articles.excerpt: Yemen's Houthis on Sunday said they launched a fresh strike on Saudi Arabia's international airport in capital Riyadh, hours after…
articles.fullText:
Yemen's Houthis on Sunday said they launched a fresh strike on Saudi Arabia's international airport in capital Riyadh, hours after the kingdom announced that flights had resumed despite repeated attacks by the Iran-backed group.

King Khalid International Airport's website showed several domestic and international flights scheduled on Sunday, including arrivals to the kingdom from Dubai, Paris and Cairo, while tracking website Flightradar24 showed some flights departed, though most were cancelled.

The renewed operations at the airport came as explosions rattled Riyadh early Sunday, after a text message was sent to residents warning of a hostile threat targeting the city.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree later said the group had "conducted three military operations with dozens of ballistic missiles," Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said on X, claiming the strike on the airport "achieved its target".

The Houthis have carried out waves of strikes on the airport, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.

Saudi authorities have not commented on a new airport attack.

Saree added that the Houthis targeted King Khalid air base in Khamis Mushait and a naval base in Jazan in the kingdom's south.

The Riyadh airport closure was a major blow for Saudi Arabia, with the kingdom's flagship investment conference postponed until 2027 as residents scrambled to find alternatives to enter and exit the country.

The prestigious motor sport race, the Dakar Rally, also added its name to a long list of events to be cancelled, postponed or relocated amid the fallout from the war.

Saree had earlier warned that Riyadh airport was still "unsafe" and a "military target".

"The Yemeni Armed Forces warn all international, regional and local airlines – as well as staff and travellers – against using King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, as it is unsafe and serves as a military target for our forces," he said.

"The Saudi regime shall bear the consequences of any operations at the airport."

Later on Sunday, Saree said Saudi Arabia had struck Yemen 56 times over the previous 24 hours.

"During the past 24 hours, Saudi warplanes launched 56 airstrikes and missiles targeting civilian objects in the governorates of Hajjah, Lahj, Amran, Saada, Al-Jawf, Taiz and Ibb using F-15 and 'Typhoon' planes that took off from the bases of Khamis Mushait and Taif, and missiles from Najran," he said on X.

As operations at the airport restarted, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis arrived in Riyadh and met with Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

During the meeting, Mitsotakis "responded favourably to the kingdom's request to keep the Patriot system in Saudi Arabia, given the current challenging circumstances", his office said.

Greece has deployed a battery to operate the US-made Patriot air defence system in Yanbu, a major oil export hub on the Red Sea coast.

Earlier, the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted at least 10 ballistic missiles.

The kingdom's civil defence agency later said two people were injured in the south by falling debris, also reporting damage to several buildings and vehicles. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Serbia's Vucic ousted in parliament poll
articles.excerpt: Serbia's student-led movement declared victory in parliamentary elections on Sunday, ending 14 years in power for Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing populist…
articles.fullText:
Serbia's student-led movement declared victory in parliamentary elections on Sunday, ending 14 years in power for Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing populist party.

The victory in the snap vote comes after nearly two years of anti-government protests sparked by the 2024 collapse of a canopy at Novi Sad railway station that killed 16 people.

The disaster has been widely blamed on corruption and triggered some of Serbia's largest protests since the fall of Slobodan Milosevic in 2000.

"Preliminary results show that students are convincingly leading in almost all polling stations," Radomir Saicic, a candidate for the Students' List, said in a speech at the movement's election HQ.

"Students won and with them also a hope that Serbia can be a country of justice, freedom and dignity."

Voters cast ballots in huge numbers on Sunday, with the country recording its highest parliamentary election turnout in more than three decades.

Vucic conceded defeat less than two hours after polls closed, triggering raucous scenes in the capital as supporters of the movement celebrated the defeat of a government they blamed for deep-rooted corruption.

"I feel incredible," student Mila Martic told AFP from the List's headquarters. "I feel as though I am finally living in a free country."

Thousands poured into the capital's streets to celebrate the victory, with passing cars honking, crowds chanting, and fireworks lighting up the skyline.

According to the country's election officials, nearly 65 percent of its 6.4 million registered voters had cast their ballots by 6.00 pm local time, two hours before polls closed.

The figure surpassed the 1993 parliamentary election, when just over 61 percent voted.

During his speech to supporters, Vucic said preliminary figures suggested the student movement could win between 135 and 140 seats, handing it an outright majority in the 250-seat parliament.

The 56-year-old statesman blamed foreign powers for the result.

"I want people to know, this was the validation of a revolution carried out with the direct support of various European countries and the US deep state, the one that is also against President Trump," he said.

For nearly two years, students have staged rallies and marched across the Balkan nation to reach voters directly and counter the media machine of Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party.

Their protests have drawn huge crowds, a final pre-election rally in Belgrade on Thursday attracting around 150,000 people, according to an independent protest monitor.

"A two-year-long dream has come true," Mirjana Nikolic, a candidate on the Students' List, said shortly after the win was announced.

Most of the student list's 250 candidates are experts from fields including academia and the arts with little political experience.

The movement has a broad platform, centred on a pledge to fight corruption.

It evolved from demands for a transparent investigation into the Novi Sad tragedy into calls for an early election.

Despite pushing back against the movement for almost two years, Vucic under mounting pressure, called the vote last month, citing "major turbulence on the domestic political scene".

The right-wing populist leader resigned the presidency to run for prime minister.

Domestic and international observers were monitoring the vote, with students mobilising large numbers of volunteers to oversee the process. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: CE meets environment minister
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee met Minister of Ecology & Environment Huang Runqiu at Government House today to exchange views on…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee met Minister of Ecology & Environment Huang Runqiu at Government House today to exchange views on deepening green co-operation. Mr Lee welcomed Mr Huang and his delegation to Hong Kong to officiate at the Belt & Road Green Innovation Conference 2026.

Mr Lee thanked the country for its support for Hong Kong as a platform for international exchanges. He also expressed gratitude for choosing the city as the venue for the conference, which is being held outside the Mainland for the first time.

He pointed out that under the "one country, two systems" principle, Hong Kong enjoys the unique advantage of connecting the Mainland and the world. Mr Lee added that the city plays the roles of "super connector" and "super value-adder" to proactively build itself into an international green co-operation hub.

The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government will build a pool of talent in international environmental protection and facilitate technology exchanges to promote the green and high-quality development of the Belt & Road (B&R) Initiative. This will be achieved through the B&R Green Development Co-operation Platform established with the Ministry of Ecology & Environment, and the B&R Sustainable Green Development Training Centre established by the Environmental Protection Department.

Mr Lee noted that the Hong Kong SAR Government attaches great importance to green and sustainable development, and added that four binding indicators have been set out in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan relating to environmental protection.

Through developing zero-carbon energy and hydrogen energy, alongside enhancing waste reduction and recycling, Hong Kong is moving towards carbon neutrality. The city will also leverage its status as a centre for green and sustainable finance to actively explore cross-boundary carbon trading, supporting the country in building a carbon market with greater international influence.

The Chief Executive added that the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) is a key engine for the country's high-quality development. Hong Kong is actively enhancing its role in the GBA's green value chain to promote green development across the region.

Hong Kong has successfully facilitated the establishment of a world-leading sustainable aviation fuel production base in Dongguan. It will further strengthen collaboration in resources circulation to jointly build a “Zero Waste Bay Area” with the Mainland.

Mr Lee thanked the ministry for its continued support for Hong Kong's environmental protection work, and expressed hope that both sides will continue to strengthen collaboration to better integrate into and serve the overall national development.

Secretary for Environment & Ecology Tse Chin-wan also attended the meeting.

articles.title: CE praises HK athletes
articles.excerpt: A commendation ceremony for the Hong Kong, China Delegation to the 20th Asian Games was held today at the Kowloon…
articles.fullText:
A commendation ceremony for the Hong Kong, China Delegation to the 20th Asian Games was held today at the Kowloon Park Sports Centre.

Chief Executive John Lee officiated at the ceremony, which was jointly organised by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government and the Sports Federation & Olympic Committee of Hong Kong, China (SF&OC). He presented certificates of commendation to the medallists to honour their exceptional achievements.

Speaking at the event, Mr Lee praised the athletes, noting that their outstanding performances exemplified the hard work and dedication of countless individuals. He expressed gratitude to the Hong Kong Sports Institute (HKSI), the SF&OC, national sports associations, coaches and medical teams for their dedicated guidance and comprehensive support, which provided staunch backing for the athletes.

Mr Lee highlighted that the Hong Kong SAR Government attaches great importance to sports development. Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan, announced last month, clearly outlines directions for advancing elite sports, maintaining Hong Kong's status as a centre for major international sports events, enhancing professionalism, and developing sports as an industry, including upgrading athletes’ overall standards through the HKSI’s elite training system.

In the latest Policy Address, Mr Lee proposed supporting the HKSI in launching a new three-year Sports Executive Training Programme. The initiative aims to broaden career pathways for retired athletes and nurture professional management talent for the sports sector.

The Hong Kong, China delegation, comprising around 580 athletes, competed in 38 events and secured a record-breaking 54 medals , including 11 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. Both the gold medal count and the overall medal tally marked the delegation’s most successful performance in Asian Games history.

Other guests included Deputy Director of the Liaison Office of the Central People’s Government in the Hong Kong SAR Sun Shangwu; President of the SF&OC of Hong Kong, China, Timothy Fok; Chef de Mission of the Hong Kong, China Delegation to the 20th Asian Games Wong Po-kee; Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki; Secretary for Culture, Sports & Tourism Rosanna Law; Permanent Secretary for Culture, Sports & Tourism Vivian Sum; Under Secretary for Culture, Sports & Tourism Raistlin Lau; Commissioner for Sports Polly Chong; and Director of Leisure & Cultural Services Manda Chan.

articles.title: HK advances fintech growth
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Christopher Hui today chaired the sixth meeting of the Coordination Group on the…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Christopher Hui today chaired the sixth meeting of the Coordination Group on the Implementation of Fintech Initiatives.

During the meeting, he exchanged views with representatives from financial regulators, the fintech sector and academia on the latest developments in fintech in Hong Kong.

Mr Hui said, drawing on the valuable views of the industry representatives, the Government and financial regulators will maintain a multi-pronged approach to facilitate fintech development, including enhancing financial infrastructure, further enriching the fintech ecosystem, nurturing fintech talent, as well as strengthening connections and collaboration beyond Hong Kong.

Different aspects of fintech, including the proposed regulatory regimes for virtual asset dealing, custody, advisory and management service providers, were discussed.

The financial regulators provided updates on their progress in adopting artificial intelligence in the financial market.

The Monetary Authority briefed the meeting on the latest developments regarding Project Ensemble, the quantum preparedness of Hong Kong's banking sector, as well as the Commercial Data Interchange and Project CargoX.

The meeting also noted that Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026, themed “Fintech Nexus: Bridging the World, Building the Future”, will be held from November 2 to 6 in conjunction with the StartmeupHK Festival.

The 11th edition of this event will attract attendees from all over the world. The Financial Services & the Treasury Bureau and Invest Hong Kong will collaborate with industry stakeholders and showcase the vitality of Hong Kong's fintech ecosystem to the global market.

articles.title: Belt-Road green conference held
articles.excerpt: The Belt & Road Green Innovation Conference 2026 was held in Hong Kong today, marking the first time the city…
articles.fullText:
The Belt & Road Green Innovation Conference 2026 was held in Hong Kong today, marking the first time the city has hosted the prestigious event.

Under the theme "Partnering with the Global South on Green Transition, Advancing Sustainable Development Worldwide", the conference underscored Hong Kong’s unique position and pivotal role in driving global green development.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Chief Executive John Lee emphasised that green transformation requires visionary planning to navigate challenges and capture emerging opportunities.

With a vision to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050, Mr Lee stated that Hong Kong is closely aligned with the country's "dual carbon" goals. He noted that Hong Kong is well-positioned to provide Belt & Road partners with world-class professional services, including financing, project management and risk management for green infrastructure and sustainable development projects.

He added that Hong Kong will actively participate in the Belt & Road Conference on Science & Technology Exchange, the Ministerial Meeting on Science, Technology & Innovation, and the implementation of the Belt & Road Science, Technology & Innovation Co-operation Action Plan.

The conference was jointly organised by the Ministry of Ecology & Environment and the Environment & Ecology Bureau of the Hong Kong SAR Government.

The event gathered over 400 political and business leaders, international organisation representatives, experts and scholars from 17 Belt & Road countries and around 40 Mainland provinces and cities. Participants engaged in in-depth exchanges on green finance, green innovation and digital empowerment.

Minister of Ecology & Environment Huang Runqiu also addressed the opening ceremony.

During a morning session, Secretary for Environment & Ecology Tse Chin-wan delivered a keynote speech, highlighting that, in the face of severe climate change challenges, Hong Kong will leverage green innovation as an engine to transform technology, capital, talent and professional services into practical and low-carbon solutions.

Mr Tse added that Hong Kong will work hand in hand with Belt & Road partners to address climate challenges and promote sustainable development.

In the afternoon, Mr Tse held bilateral meetings with delegations from Myanmar, the Maldives and Bangladesh respectively. They exchanged views on combating climate change, environmental protection and strengthening inter-city co-operation.

Separately, Hong Kong's annual flagship environmental event, the 21st Eco Expo Asia , also opened today at AsiaWorld-Expo. Running from October 26 to 29, the event will open to the public for free on its final day.

articles.title: Brazil's Lula, Bolsonaro face off in nail-biter vote
articles.excerpt: Brazil held its breath on Sunday as voters went to the polls to decide between leftist leader Luiz Inacio Lula…
articles.fullText:
Brazil held its breath on Sunday as voters went to the polls to decide between leftist leader Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva or his right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.

It is the final electoral battle for Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday and is hoping to pull off a dramatic turnaround after coming in second to the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro in the first round of voting.

Final polls showed the two candidates neck-and-neck.

Sunday's runoff will determine whether Brazil remains one of Latin America's few leftist nations or joins a regional swing to the right championed by US President Donald Trump, an ally of the Bolsonaro family, though he has not openly endorsed Flavio.

Lula, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, has pitched himself as a bulwark against US interference and democratic backsliding and promised to expand social protections.

The right "wants to govern with the American flag," he said after casting his ballot in the state of Sao Paulo.

Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, has vowed to crack down on crime and slash government spending, while handing Brazil to "the Lord Jesus Christ."

"The time has come for real change," he declared after voting in Rio de Janeiro. "Brazil can't stand another four years like this."

Bolsonaro presents himself as more moderate than his firebrand father, who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup after his 2022 election loss.

Lula, revered for social welfare programs that lifted millions out of poverty, made a dramatic comeback to office in 2022 elections after a corruption scandal saw him jailed for over 18 months.

Polling stations in Brazil will close at 4.00am Hong Kong time, with results expected within hours.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Trump: Audi to invest US$4.2bn in its first US plant
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump on Saturday announced that Audi will build an automobile plant in Georgia as he tries to…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump on Saturday announced that Audi will build an automobile plant in Georgia as he tries to deliver on his promise to bolster American manufacturing in the final days before the midterm elections.

Speaking at a campaign rally in Perry, Georgia, where he sought to boost Republican candidates, Trump said Audi – the German luxury brand owned by Volkswagen – would commit US$4.2 billion in nearby Macon to begin construction on a plant that will produce 200,000 cars a year.

“Think of that. 200,000 cars a year. That’s incredible,” Trump said, crediting his aggressive and unpopular tariff policies for the company's decision to build the plant.

The announcement seemed timed to offer a last-minute boost to Republican candidates in the battleground state, including Representative Mike Collins, who is trying to unseat Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff. Trump has spent October campaigning in reliably Republican states as the party tries to hold onto its majorities in the House and Senate. Trump won Georgia in 2024 after losing it in 2020.

Trump was joined on stage by Gernot Dollner, the chairman of the board of management at Audi, who said the plant would be producing “our biggest and most premium SUVs”.

“This is a long-term investment, because we believe in the American market,” he said.

Audi, in a news release, said the plant – its first in Georgia – would create about 4,500 jobs and that construction was scheduled to begin in 2027, with production beginning in the early 2030s.

Republicans are bracing for losses in the November 3 midterm elections as they contend with an unpopular president and an electorate that is angry over high costs and the ongoing war in Iran. (AP)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Storm Boelo lashes UK, cuts power, cancels flights
articles.excerpt: Tens of thousands of homes were without power on Sunday as Storm Boelo battered northern parts of the United Kingdom…
articles.fullText:
Tens of thousands of homes were without power on Sunday as Storm Boelo battered northern parts of the United Kingdom with strong winds and heavy rain, disrupting travel services.

Boelo is Britain's second named storm of the season and quickly follows the first – Storm Austen, which brought strong gusts to southern areas of the country on Friday.

More than 82,000 properties had no electricity , industry body the Energy Networks Association said in an update.

It added that almost 350,000 customers had been reconnected since Austen hit.

An amber wind warning was in place in Scotland, where collapsed trees, fallen cables and damaged surfaces prompted road and railway track closures.

Winds gusts peaked at 135 kilometres per hour in Argyll and Bute in western Scotland, according to the Met Office weather agency.

Scotland was also under a yellow rain warning, along with northern England, with up to 80 milimetres expected in some areas, bringing a chance of flooding.

Also affected was Northern Ireland, where several flights out of Belfast were cancelled. There were also cancellations to some ferry services across the Irish Sea between Belfast and northwest England.

The Met warned that Boelo brings a danger to life from flying debris and crashing waves and that people should stay indoors as much as possible.

Meanwhile, Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, one of Europe's busiest hubs, cancelled dozens of flights on Sunday because of Boelo.

Some 90 flights were cancelled on the airport website departures page. (AFP)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Evening News on TV32 - Oct 25
articles.excerpt: Top stories for Sunday, Oct 25, 2026 - Late night congestion at the new Huanggang port prompts calls for greater…
articles.fullText:
Top stories for Sunday, Oct 25, 2026
